title: Speak: everyday sentences
description: Whole sentences you can use today. Sound first.

units.title: About you
intro: Sentences you can use the first minute you meet someone.
In Japanese the verb or ending comes last. 'Watashi wa Mike desu' is word for word 'As for me, Mike is.'
The character は is written 'ha' but said 'wa' when it marks the topic of a sentence. です (desu) is a polite 'am, is, are'. The u is almost silent, so say 'des'.

items.hint: ha-ji-me-ma-shi-te. Said only the first time you meet.
Swap maiku for your own name. 'wa' is the particle は.

items.front: よろしくおねがいします
items.hint: yo-ro-shi-ku o-ne-gai-shi-mas. Said after your name. It is a polite 'please be kind to me'.

items.front: おなまえはなんですか
items.hint: o-na-ma-e wa nan des-ka. 'nan' means what. The 'ka' makes it a question.

items.front: アメリカからきました
items.hint: 'kara' means from. Swap in your own country. ki-ma-shi-ta.

units.title: What and where
intro: Three little words carry most simple questions: nan (what), doko (where) and ikura (how much).
Add 'desu ka' to the end and you have a polite question. Your voice does not need to rise.
Kore means this, sore means that (near you), are means that over there.

items.hint: ko-re wa nan des-ka. Point at something as you say it.
so-re wa hon des. Swap hon for any noun.
toi-re wa do-ko des-ka. One of the most useful sentences you can learn.
ko-re wa i-ku-ra des-ka. Point at the item.
hai, soh des. 'sou' is a long 'oh'.

units.title: Who, when, where
intro: More question words: dare (who), nanji (what time), nanyoubi (what day of the week).
The same ending 'desu ka' makes all of them questions.

items.hint: da-re des-ka. The r is a quick tap of the tongue.
i-ma nan-ji des-ka. 'ima' means now.

items.front: きょうはなんようびですか
items.hint: kyoh wa nan-yoh-bi des-ka. 'kyou' is today.

items.front: あしたはにちようびです
items.hint: a-shi-ta wa ni-chi-yoh-bi des. Swap in any day.
ko-ko des. Short and useful when you point.

units.title: Wants and needs
intro: To ask for something, say what you want, then を (said 'o'), then 'kudasai' (please give me).
The character を is only used as this marker, and it sounds just like お.
Feelings like hungry and thirsty use 'ga' and a past form: onaka ga sukimashita, 'my stomach has emptied'.

items.hint: mi-zu o ku-da-sai. Swap mizu for what you want.
ko-re o ku-da-sai. Point at the item.

items.front: コーヒーをおねがいします
items.hint: koh-hee o o-ne-gai-shi-mas. The long vowels are held for two beats.
o-na-ka ga su-ki-ma-shi-ta.
no-do ga ka-wa-ki-ma-shi-ta.

units.title: Eating out
intro: Two phrases are said at every meal: before you eat and after.
They are not translated word for word. Think of them as 'thanks for the food' and 'thanks, that was a feast'.

items.hint: me-nyuu o ku-da-sai.

items.meaning: thanks for the food (said before eating)
items.hint: i-ta-da-ki-ma-su. Hands together, a small bow.

items.meaning: thanks for the meal (said after eating)
items.hint: go-chi-soh-sa-ma de-shi-ta. Say it to the cook when you leave.

items.front: おかいけいをおねがいします
items.hint: o-kai-kei o o-ne-gai-shi-mas.
oi-shi-kat-ta des. The small 'tt' is a held beat.

units.title: Getting around
intro: Directions use a short list of words: massugu (straight), migi (right), hidari (left).
Add 'kudasai' to turn an instruction into a polite request.

items.hint: e-ki wa do-ko des-ka. The most useful place word in Japan.

items.front: まっすぐいってください
items.hint: mas-su-gu it-te ku-da-sai. Small tsu: a held beat before the next sound.

items.front: ひだりにまがってください
items.hint: hi-da-ri ni ma-gat-te ku-da-sai. Swap hidari for migi to say right.

items.front: ここでとめてください
items.hint: ko-ko de to-me-te ku-da-sai. Handy in a taxi.
mi-chi ni ma-yoi-ma-shi-ta.

units.title: Understanding and help
intro: You will not catch everything. These sentences keep a conversation alive.
Asking for slower or repeated speech is polite and normal.

items.front: もういちどおねがいします
items.hint: moh i-chi-do o-ne-gai-shi-mas.

items.front: ゆっくりおねがいします
items.hint: yuk-ku-ri o-ne-gai-shi-mas.

items.front: えいごがわかりますか
items.hint: ei-go ga wa-ka-ri-mas-ka.

items.front: にほんごがすこしはなせます
items.meaning: I can speak a little Japanese.
items.hint: ni-hon-go ga su-ko-shi ha-na-se-mas.
ta-su-ke-te ku-da-sai.
dai-joh-bu des. Also a polite no-thanks.

units.title: Everyday talk
intro: Small talk you will hear all the time.
'Ogenki desu ka' asks how someone is. The honest answer is usually 'genki desu', I'm well.

items.hint: o-gen-ki des-ka.

items.front: げんきです、ありがとう
items.hint: gen-ki des, a-ri-ga-toh.
o-ya-su-mi-na-sai.
ta-no-shi-kat-ta des.
ma-ta a-shi-ta. Casual.
